notable_absence.finding: Despite being the single most role/privilege-dense page in this batch, manage-users-and-roles.md never once attaches the word 'privilege' to a specific named token - every concretely-named token on this page (cluster_admin, data_reader, data_writer, scope_admin, ro_admin, query_external_access, analytics_reader, admin/Full Administrator) is consistently and exclusively called a 'role' throughout. 'Privilege' appears only twice, both times in the fully abstract sense ('read and write privileges', 'define their privileges') matching rbac-model:privilege, not a concrete instance. This page shows ZERO recurrence of the round-12 misclassification pattern (roles wrongly minted as privilege:*) - worth recording as a positive confirmation for reconciliation confidence, since this is exactly the page-type (heavy role-assignment prose plus REST/CLI examples) round 12 identified as the origin of the earlier miscoding.

cross_component_finding: 'Role assignment controls the availability of the Couchbase Web Console features to an administrator. Unavailable features are hidden. Therefore, the console interface changes based on the roles assigned to the user.' (the 'Role-Based Console Appearance' section) is a genuinely new mechanism not covered by any existing predicate: Server's RBAC gates WEB CONSOLE UI VISIBILITY itself, not just data-plane/statement access. This is a different axis from Capella's requiresUiMode (Quick vs Advanced Mode, a client-side affordance gate independent of role) - here the ROLE ITSELF determines what UI surface exists at all. No relation was forced for this since no clean existing predicate fits (requiresUiMode's object is a UI-mode value, not a role) - flagged here for reconciliation to consider minting a predicate such as 'gatesUiVisibility' if this recurs.
cross_product_finding: Server's role-grant syntax uses a flat, single-tier role catalogue with an optional bucket:scope:collection bracket suffix for data-plane roles (e.g. `data_reader[testBucket:my_new_scope:my_new_collection]`) - assigned directly to a user or inherited via a single level of group membership. This is structurally simpler than Capella's role model, which layers organization-scope roles (capella-role:organization-owner, capella-role:project-creator) that imply project-scope access (impliesRole) on top of project-scope roles (capella-role:cluster-manager, capella-role:data-reader, etc.) - a two-tier hierarchy with no equivalent on the Server side documented in this batch. The two 'role' families remain, as already recorded, structurally distinct rather than layers of one system.
